hero.heading: Open code. Open ownership.
hero.subheading: The open wallet infrastructure for high-alignment users who want control, not just custody.

chains.heading: Multi-chain by design
chains.subheading: Manage assets across Solana and Bitcoin — including devnets and testnets.

why.heading: Open source is non-negotiable.
why.subheading: Closed code is a trust tax. Most wallets solve custody, but not control. Open source is the clearest way to reduce hidden power, opaque decisions, and asymmetric control at the wallet layer.

items.title: Decentralization without transparency is theater.
items.description: You do not decentralize power by saying it. You do it by exposing the rules. Without transparency, users may hold keys while still depending on closed systems that shape access, integrations, defaults, and distribution.

items.title: Security improves in public.
items.description: Closed systems fail silently. Open systems fail in public and improve faster. For users who care about resilience and verifiability, transparency is not optional.

items.title: If users do not shape it, it is not aligned.
items.description: Ownership and governance are not cosmetic layers. They are structural choices. Salmon is built for users who want a wallet layer that can evolve in the open and align with the ecosystem it serves.

features.heading: Open wallet infrastructure, already live
features.subheading: Salmon is not a theoretical alternative. It is already live across browser extension, web wallet, Android, and a public open-source repository.

items.title: Built for high-alignment users
items.description: Designed for crypto natives, builders, integrators, contributors, and communities that care about open, verifiable wallet infrastructure.

items.title: Self-custodial by design
items.description: Use core wallet flows, manage assets, and interact with the ecosystem without giving up custody of your keys.

items.title: Active Solana validator
items.description: Salmon also operates an active Solana validator, reinforcing its operational alignment with the ecosystem it is building for.

items.title: Ready to deepen integrations
items.description: The next phase is focused on reliability, mobile parity, security, and stronger ecosystem integrations across the users and projects that matter most.

items.title: Public open-source repository
items.description: Core software is available through a public repository so the wallet layer can be inspected, challenged, and improved in the open.

security.heading: Security by design
security.subheading: Built to reduce trust assumptions through transparency, testing, and disciplined execution.

items.title: Keys stay with you
items.description: Your private keys are encrypted on your device and protected by your password. Salmon is built so custody stays with the user.

items.title: Privacy with restraint
items.description: Salmon is designed to minimize unnecessary data collection and reduce hidden extraction at the interface layer. The goal is a wallet experience with fewer trust assumptions and more user control.

items.title: Open security model
items.description: Security improves through transparency. Open-source code, public review, continuous testing, and audit readiness create a stronger and more verifiable security posture.

items.title: Every change reviewed
items.description: Contributions are inspected before they become part of the wallet. Critical infrastructure should evolve through visible review and accountable engineering, not behind closed doors.

manifesto.heading: Salmon is public infrastructure.
manifesto.subheading: No hidden gatekeepers. No opaque control. Just systems that can be inspected, challenged, and improved.

principles.title: Salmon is open-source.
principles.description: Because closed code creates invisible power.

principles.title: Salmon is built for aligned ownership.
principles.description: Because the people who depend on the wallet layer should have a path to shape how it evolves.

principles.title: Salmon assumes adversaries.
principles.description: Security is earned through exposure, not secrecy.

principles.title: Salmon prioritizes longevity over growth.
principles.description: A wallet that earns trust over time is more valuable than one that only optimizes for short-term growth.

principles.title: If Salmon fails, it should fail in public.
principles.description: If it succeeds, it should remain open to the ecosystem that helped build it.

items.question: What is Salmon?
items.answer: Salmon is an open-source, self-custodial wallet built as open wallet infrastructure. It is designed for users, builders, and contributors who want control without depending on closed wallet-layer decisions.

items.question: Does Salmon have access to my private keys?
items.answer: No. Your private keys are encrypted locally on your device and remain under your control. If you lose your recovery phrase, no one can recover it for you.

items.question: What makes Salmon different from other wallets?
items.answer: Most wallets give users custody, but still keep roadmap decisions, integrations, defaults, and product evolution under private control. Salmon is built differently: open-source, verifiable, and aligned with the ecosystem it serves.

items.question: Is Salmon really open-source?
items.answer: Yes. Salmon’s core software is open-source and available through its public repository. The goal is not only to make the code visible, but to keep the wallet layer transparent and verifiable.

items.question: What chains does Salmon support?
items.answer: Salmon is built initially around Solana and is expanding toward Bitcoin and additional networks where demand and alignment are strongest.

items.question: Can I use Salmon today?
items.answer: Yes. Salmon is already live across browser extension, web wallet, and Android, with continued work toward stronger mobile parity and deeper ecosystem integrations.

items.question: Does Salmon operate beyond the wallet itself?
items.answer: Yes. Salmon also operates an active Solana validator, reinforcing its role as infrastructure aligned with the ecosystem it serves.

items.question: Does Salmon collect user data?
items.answer: Salmon is designed to reduce unnecessary data collection and hidden extraction at the interface layer. For implementation details and current policy, see the Privacy Policy.

items.question: What happens if Salmon stops operating?
items.answer: Salmon is open-source infrastructure. Even if the original team disappears, the code remains accessible and the project can continue to evolve in the open rather than disappear behind a closed company structure.

items.question: Is Salmon audited?
items.answer: Salmon follows an open security model built around reviews, continuous testing, and audit readiness. Security is treated as an ongoing process, not a one-time marketing claim.

items.question: Who controls Salmon?
items.answer: Salmon is being built so the wallet layer does not remain dependent on private control alone. The direction is toward governance and ownership structures that can align the project with the community and ecosystem it serves.
